findings.finding: Two open issuance channels can be drawn on any day, including tonight or 2026-10-08. The first is the 2026 Stock Incentive Plan S-8 filed and effective 2026-09-11: 5,087,548 pre-split Class A shares, about 203.5k after the split and about 20% of the 1,017,510 Class A issued. It has no reoffer prospectus, so grants to non-affiliate consultants become tradable shares. The second is the $200M F-3 shelf, effective 2026-09-10, which the company used for a dilutive offering in July 2026.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Both registrations are effective now, so stock can be issued and sold into the 2026-10-08 session with no further SEC step. The company has issued equity repeatedly in 2026: units with zero-price warrants in July, Class B to the CEO in September, and the White Lion equity line agreed in August 2025. Nothing dates a specific draw inside the window, which is why this is sized small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the July 2026 zero-price-warrant units (up to 24M pre-split shares) and the 2026-09-03 collapse, the stock fell on 10 of its 11 subsequent large-fall next sessions (baseline history.events, 2026-09-03 to 2026-10-06), with a median of about -9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The price holds a fall that has already happened. If the market priced an issuance landing tonight, a dated 6-K or a pricing release would exist. None does, so any draw on 2026-10-08 would be new supply into roughly a million-share Class A float. The size stays small because the timing is inferred.
findings.independence: The F-3 shelf (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2018529/000121390026089705/ea0296968-f3_intercont.htm, 2026-08-14, effective 2026-09-10) and the July 424B4 zero-price warrant structure (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2018529/000121390026075881/ea0291199-05.htm) show the issuer's habit of issuing. Both are the issuer's own filings, so this is not independent of the company.

outside_window.finding: The 8,000,000 July 2026 warrants expire about six months after the 2026-07-08 issue, around 2027-01-08. Most appear already exercised: Class A grew to 25.4M before the September split.
The 180-day lock-up for officers, directors and certain holders from the July offering ends around 2027-01-04.

There were two 25-for-1 reverse splits in 2026 (2026-04-02 and 2026-09-17). A renewed bid-price deficiency would likely get no cure period under Nasdaq's reverse-split limits, but the rule text was not sourced here. The stock is at $1.33, so no deficiency can arise inside the window.

The CEO's vehicle bought 1,625,000 Class B at $0.40 pre-split (about $10 post-split), closed 2026-09-25 for $650,000. This shows commitment, but it was completed and public before the fall, with no in-window mechanism.
